decisions.reason: As a recent multi-model extension of the firm’s core office offer, it fits the move toward flexible workplaces and, with the firm hiring and investing in R&D, there is enough slack to keep it absent clear signs of underperformance.
This chair family is close to the established portfolio and was given its own page, so without evidence of a result shortfall relative to aspirations management would likely continue it.

The floor-cushion line is more niche and demand is less certain, but it still builds on the firm’s materials and interior-solutions capabilities, so available organisational slack makes retention more likely than withdrawal.

Although the sofa is close to the core business, its weaker website prominence suggests less commitment or traction, making it the most vulnerable product, but the firm would still likely give it more time before reallocating resources.

The high standing table closely matches the firm’s commercial-interior positioning and contemporary workspace trends, so it is likely to stay while management evaluates it against aspirations over a longer period.

Even though the rug collection is more distant from the established offer, its flagship status and role in the firm’s strategic direction toward broader interior solutions make management likely to retain it for at least another year.
